C01.rationale: Acting identity, business, scopes and connection are described; the own non-secret profile updates through the account page service. Password change and identity verification stay browser-only by design.

C02.rationale: Search, read, create, update, archive/activate and export share BusinessService with the tenant screens, including slug and pattern rules and the optional owner invitation. Creation and archive are operator-only.

C03.rationale: Access requests are submitted with the public abuse controls and reviewed by operators; approval changes the application only, and provisioning stays a separate business_create.

C04.rationale: Both dashboards read the same DashboardService metrics, upcoming and today bookings and setup readiness as the UI, with the business timezone boundaries.

C05.rationale: Pattern-aware list, detail and bounded CSV export with the UI filters and stable cursor paging, per business and across granted businesses for operators.

C06.rationale: Staff creation for all four patterns runs the manual-booking validation, inventory lock and notifications behind a reviewed preview.

C07.rationale: Legal transitions come from the same transition table as the admin status action; restoring transitions recheck inventory and keep reminder and email behaviour.

C08.rationale: Staff and customer moves preview and commit for every pattern, keep original and replacement history and the customer deadlines distinct from staff authority.

C09.rationale: Customer cancellation describes eligibility, cancels once under a manage grant bound to the booking and business, and returns the receipt and notification state.

C10.rationale: calendar_summary returns the day, week or month the admin calendar shows: the week starts on the business’s week start, the month is the 42-cell grid, and each day carries the occupied-booking count, closure and opening state. CalendarController and calendar_summary share BookingCalendar for the window, the paged booking load and groupOccupiedDates. calendar_get pages the booking records behind any range of up to 93 days.

C11.rationale: Search, detail, history and export follow the customer screens with field minimisation; there is deliberately no customer-edit operation because the UI has none.

C12.rationale: Services share CatalogService with the service forms, including staff assignments, explicit active state and versioned updates.

C13.rationale: Staff share CatalogService with the staff forms, including service assignment and explicit active state; images go through media_upload_prepare (C21).

C14.rationale: Weekly rules, staff overrides and reset-to-business schedule are configuration operations, kept separate from computed availability (C30).

C15.rationale: Blocks are listed, added and removed with pattern-aware targets; the preview names affected bookings and never cancels them.

C16.rationale: Resources, stay bounds, check-in/out days and seasonal rates share the resource forms; range price comes from availability_search. There is no resource delete because the UI has none.

C17.rationale: Capacity slots are listed, created, toggled and deleted like the UI; there is no edit or per-slot price operation because the UI has none.

C18.rationale: Events with recurrence, exclusions, capacity, spot bounds, location, pricing and waitlist settings share the event forms; occurrences come from availability_search.

C19.rationale: The waitlist maps to existing operations, with no dedicated tool. bookings_list with status=waitlisted and event_id (sort=id, direction=asc) lists an event’s waitlist in arrival order. booking_status_set from waitlisted to confirmed promotes under the inventory lock after trusted review, is refused with inventory_conflict while the event is full, and queues the promotion email to the customer only. A prospective customer joins a full event’s waitlist through public_booking_create, with consent recorded only on the customer’s review page; joining never overbooks.

C20.rationale: General and regional settings read and change the same fields as the settings tab; consequential changes need a reviewed preview.

C21.rationale: Branding fields and logo media use the branding tab rules; uploads use single-purpose grants with the same file limits. There is no business-cover editor because the UI has none.

C22.rationale: Confirmation text, cancellation policy, phone requirement, approval mode and cancel/reschedule permissions read and change through the booking-page tab rules for all patterns.

C23.rationale: Advance limits, horizon, daily customer limit and timeslot step/buffer use the booking tab rules and stay gated to the patterns that screen supports.

C24.rationale: Privacy policy, consent and retention settings use the privacy tab rules with a reviewed preview; historical consent records are untouched.

C25.rationale: Notification recipients and preferences use the notifications tab rules; delivery state is reported on each write receipt.

C26.rationale: Template overrides, restore-to-default and synthetic previews share the email settings service; there is no mass-mail operation.

C27.rationale: Embed settings and the exact credential-free snippet come from the embed tab service with the derived host and business.

C28.rationale: List, invite and activate/deactivate follow the team screen under owner/operator policy, protect the last owner and never elevate a role through scopes.

C29.rationale: Tenant-specific discovery of pattern, catalog and public policy matches the booking page; private and archived businesses stay undiscoverable.

C30.rationale: All four calculators back public, staff and customer availability with the same timezone, staff, party, occurrence and reschedule rules as the booking page.

C31.rationale: Prospective customers preview and create through the booking-page rules, with browser-recorded consent, approval and waitlist outcomes and a safe manage handoff. A confirmed result, and the customer’s own booking read, carry a calendar object with the booking page’s Google Calendar link and iCalendar file, built by CalendarLinks in the same format as the page’s client-side actions. Pending and waitlisted results carry calendar: null.

C32.rationale: Required fields, preparation text, virtual and timezone behaviour and consent text are discovered from the public operations and validated by the shared booking draft.

C33.rationale: Verified customers read, export and request deletion of their own data under a privacy grant separate from booking management; there is no directory search by email.

C34.rationale: The operator queue, review, dismiss and irreversible confirm share the deletion queue service; confirmation is bound to the exact affected data.

C35.rationale: Redacted settings reads and non-secret updates share the settings screen; secrets report configured state only, and credential entry is an exact browser handoff.

C36.rationale: Health, last and next run and failures are reported; run-now queues a durable request that shares the cron dispatcher and overlap lock, and never returns the cron secret.

C37.rationale: Privileged, redacted and filtered audit reads and exports carry principal, connection, action, result and correlation; raw logs are a controlled operator handoff.

C38.rationale: Agents read sanitized version and update readiness and receive a prepared handoff. Installing updates, installation credentials and arbitrary archives stay trusted human and host operations.

C39.rationale: Operators resolve an explicit business context while keeping their own attribution; no impersonation cookie or browser session is created.

C40.rationale: A connection describes itself, tests itself, lists its own activity, brings its own expiry forward and revokes itself; the last two need the represented person’s browser review. connection_test reports whether the credential authenticates, its principal, businesses, scopes, expiry, transport and negotiated protocol, and which actions the role allows but the grant lacks. connection_expire mirrors the admin screen, which fixes expiry at creation and revokes: it may only shorten, never extend, and caps every token at the new end. Creating grants, showing a secret once and rotating raw tokens stay browser-only by design; connection_setup points there. Per-operation HTTP and MCP evidence is tracked in the operations ledger.

C41.rationale: A new enabling feature, not an existing-UI parity claim: signed business events, subscription management, delivery diagnostics and retries, and receipt status and recovery.

C42.rationale: capabilities_get lists the actor-visible operations, server version and supported protocol versions, and the generated OpenAPI and MCP tool catalog come from the same registry. Failures name their cause: unknown_endpoint (404, with discovery_url) for a wrong address under /api/agent/v2 or /mcp, authorization_required for a missing header, unauthorized for an unknown token, wrong_audience, connection_revoked, connection_expired, account_disabled (403), insufficient_scope (403, also as an MCP tool error for hidden tools) and unsupported_protocol_version in the MCP -32022 error data. connection_test is the authenticated self-check and reports scope coverage.
